title: Solve Percent and Percent Change Problems with Desmos
description: Translate percent statements into equations, use Desmos percent-of notation with regression, apply the percent-change template, and solve multi-step percent problems.

questions.explanation_html: Use the equation amount = 35/100 × 180. Its value is \(63\).
questions.variation: Solve for a percent, a part, or a base

questions.stem_html: A quantity of 250 units increased by 18%. What was the new quantity?
questions.explanation_html: Use the original 250 as the base of the change. The multiplier is 118/100, yielding \(295\).
questions.variation: Use the starting value to compute a percent increase or decrease

questions.stem_html: After a price decreased by 25%, the price was \(210\) dollars. What was the original price in dollars?
questions.explanation_html: The known new price is the original price times 75/100. Fit the original price or divide by this factor to get 280.
questions.variation: Recover an unknown original amount after a change

questions.stem_html: One shelf has \(68\) books, which is 20% fewer than the number on a second shelf. How many books are on the second shelf?
questions.explanation_html: The second shelf is the comparison base because it comes after “than.” Its count multiplied by 80/100 gives \(68\); the count is 85.
questions.variation: Identify the comparison base in percent-more or percent-fewer claims

questions.stem_html: A ticket was discounted by 20% from its original price. A fixed 7-dollar fee was then added, for a final price of \(43\) dollars. What was the original ticket price in dollars?
questions.explanation_html: Define discounted price as the original multiplied by 80/100. Fit discounted price + 7 = \(43\). The discounted price is \(36\) and the original is 45.
questions.variation: Use a definition to connect a discount and a fixed charge

questions.stem_html: \(56\) is what percent of 350? Enter the number without the percent sign.

questions.explanation_html: Put the unknown on the base side, so \(36=(24/100)b\). Fitting or dividing yields 150.
